summary: On 2 June 2026, Claude experienced a partial outage lasting roughly four hours and forty-nine minutes, with elevated model errors, hanging responses and effects reported across Claude chat and Claude Code. During the outage, the free-plan interface attributed inability to respond to unexpected capacity constraints and suggested upgrading to Pro. Separate reporting described unusually rapid quota depletion for some paid Pro and Max users and a quota reset for affected accounts.

taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: Full occurrence-led review against VIGIL Failure Taxonomy 0.6.6 retains VIGIL-FC-000032 Access-State Collapse on a narrower evidentiary basis. During a provider-confirmed partial outage and elevated model errors, the free-plan interface represented inability to respond as unexpected capacity constraints and suggested upgrading to Pro. Provider service failure, model-specific error and plan capacity are materially distinct access causes with different recovery paths; directing the user toward a paid-plan upgrade during the outage omitted the distinction needed for correct handling. Separate reporting of anomalously depleted paid quotas and a remedial reset corroborates that quota state also became unreliable, but the unverified proposed sub-agent cause is not adopted. VIGIL-FC-000031 Authentication-State Continuity Failure is rejected because no authentication-state transition propagation defect is evidenced. VIGIL-FC-000048 Verification-Dependency Access Failure is rejected because no dependent identity, licence, eligibility or entitlement verifier is shown to have failed.

classification_review_provenance.authority_boundary: Taxonomy version reviewed: 0.6.6. Accepted mapping: VIGIL-FC-000032, based on the directly observed capacity-and-upgrade representation during a provider-confirmed partial outage. The separately reported quota reset is corroborative rather than necessary to the mapping. Rejected: VIGIL-FC-000031 because no authentication transition propagation defect is established; VIGIL-FC-000048 because no qualifying verification dependency is identified. The reported Claude Code sub-agent mechanism is not treated as established root cause.

assessment_boundaries: The historical incident-specific Claude Status page was not available through a stable discoverable URL; the provider updates are preserved through contemporaneous reporting and screenshots.
The Economic Times' proposed Claude Code sub-agent mechanism is attributed to user reports and is not treated as an established provider root cause.

Downdetector counts do not establish the total affected population, and no unreported loss from interrupted work is inferred.
vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Contemporaneous reporting places the partial outage from about 07:10 to 11:59 GMT on 2 June 2026. Claude Status reported elevated errors and implementation of a fix; the reporter observed hanging responses across Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 and a free-plan message attributing inability to respond to unexpected capacity constraints while suggesting an upgrade to Pro. Separate reporting described some Pro and Max users' quotas depleting within minutes and a reset for affected accounts.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The incident exposed multiple operational states—provider outage, model error, plan capacity and consumed quota—but the interface directed at least one outage-affected path toward a plan-upgrade interpretation. That representation mattered because paying for a higher tier was not the recovery action for a provider-side outage. Access-state governance requires service availability, model availability, entitlement and quota state to remain distinguishable and auditable under degraded conditions.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: INC-000023 shows why economic and continuity controls must share a reliable state model. Upgrade prompts and quota enforcement should be suppressed or qualified when the provider cannot distinguish genuine plan exhaustion from incident-induced failure. The mapping remains bounded to the observed misrepresentation; ordinary capacity constraints and outages do not by themselves constitute Access-State Collapse.

clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A provider-side availability incident and a model-specific error must remain identifiable as operational service states rather than being silently converted into an account or plan restriction.

clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Provider unavailability, genuine free-tier capacity exhaustion and paid-plan eligibility are different states with different recovery paths; an upgrade prompt must not represent provider failure as user-plan insufficiency.

dimensions.assessment_basis: Contemporaneous reporting documents a multi-hour partial outage affecting conversational and coding workflows, with direct observations of hanging responses and separate reports of unusable paid-plan quota. The duration exceeds two hours and the evidence identifies material disruption of important developer workflows with bounded recovery. The record does not claim complete service unavailability or convert self-reported outage counts into a verified population threshold. Threshold applied: Material disruption of an important service or organisational workflow; a critical or important function unavailable for more than two hours; complete relevant cloud-service unavailability over 30 minutes; or limited availability affecting over five percent or one million EU users, whichever is smaller, for over one hour, with bounded recovery.
